<!--
Template for kind: "fiction" chapters.

A chapter is a story or scene, not a lesson. There is no "principle" to
extract, no numbered techniques, no pitfalls, no Quick reference. Write
free-form Marathi prose.

Length and chapter count:
- 800-2500 words is a reasonable range per chapter; longer is OK if the
  story demands it. Stay phone-readable — avoid single chapters past
  ~3000 words.
- Chapter count is variable. A short-story collection might be 6 chapters;
  a serialized novella might be 15+. Match what the story needs, not a
  fixed number.

Universal rules (CLAUDE.md):
- Devanagari prose with Roman loanwords as people actually speak
  (no टॅन्ट्रम).
- Marathi-context settings — joint family, बस stop, kitchen, festival prep,
  exam season, school, neighbours. Concrete sensory detail.
- Original story. Do not retell a published work.
- DO NOT include "## Quick reference", "## ही techniques वापरा",
  "## हे टाळा", or numbered technique lists. Those are for howto only.

What works:
- Open with action or dialogue, not a setup paragraph.
- Use specific Marathi household detail to ground every scene.
- Keep dialogue in Devanagari + Roman loanwords, the same way the rest of
  the site does.
- Use "## <heading>" only if you genuinely need a section break (time-skip,
  POV change). Continuous prose with paragraph breaks is the default.
- A short reflective beat at the end is fine — write it as prose, not as
  a card.

Before drafting the book's chapters, plan opening-scene-type, insight-source,
and resolution-mechanic per chapter so scenes/stories don't converge on one
default shape across the book. See CLAUDE.md → "Structural variety across
chapters" for the full menu.
-->

<Opening scene — drop the reader directly into the moment. Dialogue, action,
or a sharp piece of household detail. Avoid "Aniket was a man who...".>

<Continue the scene. Show through dialogue and action what the characters
want, what's at stake, what's getting in the way. Marathi household texture
throughout — the smell of ओली earth before पाऊस, the sound of the cooker
whistle, the बस conductor's call.>

## <Optional section break heading — only if the story shifts time, place,
   or POV. Otherwise just leave a blank line and continue.>

<Next beat. Build to a turn — something changes for the character, even if
the change is small (a realization, a decision, a hesitation).>

<Closing paragraph. Land the chapter on a moment, not a moral. Resist the
urge to spell out the lesson — trust the reader.>
